# Set Up

## Load Libraries

```{r library}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(knitr)
  library(openxlsx)
})

base_dir <- rprojroot::find_root(
  rprojroot::has_dir("AD_CR_HRS"), path = getwd()
)
analysis_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "AD_CR_HRS")
save_dir <- file.path(analysis_dir, "analysis-results", "ADNI")
```

# Define Functions

## Reduced Model Results Table

```{r func_results_table}
reduced_result_table <- function(model, group_name) {
  # Stop before exporting an incomplete fixed-effect model.
  if (anyNA(lme4::fixef(model, add.dropped = TRUE))) {
    stop(
      group_name,
      ": the Reduced Model has non-estimable fixed effects. ",
      "Resolve these before exporting the table."
    )
  }

  coef_matrix <- stats::coef(summary(model, ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
  required_columns <- c("Estimate", "Std. Error", "t value", "Pr(>|t|)")
  if (!all(required_columns %in% colnames(coef_matrix))) {
    stop(group_name, ": expected lmerTest coefficient columns were not found.")
  }

  data.frame(
    Term = rownames(coef_matrix),
    Estimate = unname(coef_matrix[, "Estimate"]),
    StdErr = unname(coef_matrix[, "Std. Error"]),
    tValue = unname(coef_matrix[, "t value"]),
    `P-value` = unname(coef_matrix[, "Pr(>|t|)"]),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Significance = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.finite(.data[["P-value"]]) ~ "-",
        .data[["P-value"]] < 0.001 ~ "***",
        .data[["P-value"]] < 0.01 ~ "**",
        .data[["P-value"]] < 0.05 ~ "*",
        TRUE ~ ""
      )
    )
}
```

## Excel Sheet Text

```{r func_excel_text}
make_reduced_model_caption <- function(model, group_name, mrs_median) {
  n_participants <- length(unique(stats::model.frame(model)$RID))
  n_observations <- stats::nobs(model)
  split_description <- if (identical(group_name, "High MRS")) {
    "MRS z-score >"
  } else {
    "MRS z-score <="
  }

  paste0(
    "ADNI reduced linear mixed-effects model in the ", group_name,
    " group (N = ", n_participants, " participants; ", n_observations,
    " observations). Outcome: PHC_MEM. The model includes baseline age, ",
    "sex, APOE4, education, continuous MRS, baseline pTau, time, and all ",
    "three pairwise interactions among MRS, pTau, and time, with a ",
    "participant-specific random intercept. Time is in years. MRS and ",
    "baseline age use pooled participant-level z-scores; pTau retains ",
    "its input-data scale. ", group_name, ": ", split_description, " ",
    format(mrs_median, digits = 6), " (pooled participant-level median)."
  )
}

make_reduced_model_footnote <- function() {
  paste0(
    "*** P-value < 0.001; ** P-value < 0.01; * P-value < 0.05. ",
    "Two-sided P-values use Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; models ",
    "are fitted using REML. Term names match the R model output."
  )
}
```

## Excel Sheet Layout

```{r func_excel_layout}
write_excel_caption <- function(wb, sheet, caption) {
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet, caption, startCol = 2, startRow = 1)
  openxlsx::mergeCells(wb, sheet, cols = 2:7, rows = 1)
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, openxlsx::createStyle(wrapText = TRUE, valign = "top"),
    rows = 1, cols = 2
  )
  openxlsx::setRowHeights(wb, sheet, rows = 1, heights = 110)
}

write_excel_results_table <- function(wb, sheet, result_table) {
  header_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(
    textDecoration = "bold", fgFill = "#E7E6E6", halign = "center",
    border = c("top", "bottom"), borderStyle = "thin"
  )
  openxlsx::writeData(
    wb, sheet, result_table, startCol = 2, startRow = 2,
    rowNames = FALSE, headerStyle = header_style, keepNA = FALSE
  )
}

write_excel_footnote <- function(wb, sheet, footnote, row) {
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet, footnote, startCol = 2, startRow = row)
  openxlsx::mergeCells(wb, sheet, cols = 2:7, rows = row)
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet,
    openxlsx::createStyle(fontSize = 10, wrapText = TRUE, valign = "top"),
    rows = row, cols = 2
  )
  openxlsx::setRowHeights(wb, sheet, rows = row, heights = 32)
}
```

## Excel Cell Styles

```{r func_excel_style}
style_excel_body <- function(wb, sheet, last_row) {
  body_rows <- seq.int(3L, last_row)

  # Estimate, StdErr, and tValue
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0.000", halign = "right"),
    rows = body_rows, cols = 3:5, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
  )
  # P-value
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0.00E+00", halign = "right"),
    rows = body_rows, cols = 6, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
  )
  # Significance
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, openxlsx::createStyle(halign = "center"),
    rows = body_rows, cols = 7, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
  )
}

style_excel_borders <- function(wb, sheet, last_row) {
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, openxlsx::createStyle(border = "left", borderStyle = "thin"),
    rows = 2:last_row, cols = 2, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
  )
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, openxlsx::createStyle(border = "right", borderStyle = "thin"),
    rows = 2:last_row, cols = 7, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
  )
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, openxlsx::createStyle(border = "bottom", borderStyle = "thin"),
    rows = last_row, cols = 2:7, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
  )
}

set_excel_dimensions <- function(wb, sheet, last_row) {
  openxlsx::setRowHeights(wb, sheet, rows = 2:last_row, heights = 20)
  openxlsx::setColWidths(
    wb, sheet, cols = 1:7, widths = c(3, 35, 14, 14, 13, 15, 16)
  )
}

set_excel_print_options <- function(wb, sheet) {
  openxlsx::freezePane(wb, sheet, firstActiveRow = 3, firstActiveCol = 3)
  openxlsx::pageSetup(
    wb, sheet, orientation = "landscape", fitToWidth = 1, fitToHeight = 1
  )
}
```

## Write Excel

```{r func_excel}
write_reduced_model_excel <- function(
    model, result_table, group_name, mrs_median, path
) {
  sheet <- "Model results"
  last_row <- nrow(result_table) + 2L

  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet, gridLines = FALSE)
  openxlsx::modifyBaseFont(wb, fontName = "Calibri", fontSize = 11)

  write_excel_caption(
    wb, sheet, make_reduced_model_caption(model, group_name, mrs_median)
  )
  write_excel_results_table(wb, sheet, result_table)
  style_excel_body(wb, sheet, last_row)
  style_excel_borders(wb, sheet, last_row)
  set_excel_dimensions(wb, sheet, last_row)
  write_excel_footnote(
    wb, sheet, make_reduced_model_footnote(), row = last_row + 2L
  )
  set_excel_print_options(wb, sheet)

  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, file = path, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

# Load Data

```{r load}
prep_ls <- readRDS(file.path(save_dir, "ADNI_Split.rds"))
mrs_model_df <- prep_ls$mrs_model_df
mrs_median <- prep_ls$mrs_median
mrs_levels <- prep_ls$mrs_levels
mrs_low_df <- prep_ls$mrs_low_df
mrs_high_df <- prep_ls$mrs_high_df
mrs_datasets <- prep_ls$mrs_datasets
```

# Fit the Reduced Model in Each Dataset

Each model retains the **Reduced Model** formula from the previous file:

- all three two-way interactions
    - `mrs_z:time`
    - `baseline_pTau:time`
    - `mrs_z:baseline_pTau`
- the original covariates
- a participant random intercept.

Both MRS and baseline pTau remain continuous within each dataset; the three-way
interaction is omitted.

Within each MRS dataset:

- `baseline_pTau:time` estimates the difference in annual memory slope per
one-unit higher baseline pTau on its input-data
scale.
- `mrs_z:time` estimates the annual memory-slope difference per one SD higher
MRS on the original pooled scale.

Separate within-group P values do not test whether pTau-associated slopes differ
between the two MRS groups.

## Define Model

```{r reduced_model_formula}
reduced_formula <- stats::as.formula(
  paste(
    "PHC_MEM ~ baseline_age_z",
    "PHC_Sex",
    "APOE4",
    "PHC_Education",
    "mrs_z",
    "baseline_pTau",
    "mrs_z*time",
    "baseline_pTau*time",
    "mrs_z*baseline_pTau",
    "(1 | RID)",
    sep = " + "
  )
)

# Check that each dataset supports the requested model before fitting.
for (group_name in mrs_levels) {
  group_df <- mrs_datasets[[group_name]]
  if (
    dplyr::n_distinct(group_df$RID) < 2L ||
    nrow(group_df) <= dplyr::n_distinct(group_df$RID)
  ) {
    stop(group_name, ": insufficient repeated observations for a random intercept.")
  }

  for (column in c("mrs_z", "baseline_pTau", "time")) {
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(group_df[[column]]) < 2L) {
      stop(group_name, ": ", column, " has no within-group variation.")
    }
  }

  if (max(group_df$time) <= 0) {
    stop(group_name, ": no positive follow-up time.")
  }

  for (column in c("PHC_Sex", "APOE4")) {
    if (is.factor(group_df[[column]]) && nlevels(group_df[[column]]) < 2L) {
      stop(group_name, ": factor ", column, " has only one observed level.")
    }
  }
}
```

## Low MRS

```{r reduced_low_mrs}
sf_low <- lmerTest::lmer(
  reduced_formula,
  data = mrs_low_df,
  REML = TRUE,
  na.action = stats::na.fail
)
cat("Reduced Model: Low MRS\n")
summary(sf_low)
```

## High MRS

```{r reduced_high_mrs}
sf_high <- lmerTest::lmer(
  reduced_formula,
  data = mrs_high_df,
  REML = TRUE,
  na.action = stats::na.fail
)
cat("Reduced Model: High MRS\n")
summary(sf_high)
```

## Export to Excel

```{r export_reduced_model_excel}
# Validate both result tables before writing either workbook.
high_mrs_results <- reduced_result_table(sf_high, "High MRS")
low_mrs_results <- reduced_result_table(sf_low, "Low MRS")
reduced_excel_paths <- c(
  `High MRS` = file.path(save_dir, "ADNI_reduced_model_high_MRS.xlsx"),
  `Low MRS` = file.path(save_dir, "ADNI_reduced_model_low_MRS.xlsx")
)
write_reduced_model_excel(
  sf_high,
  high_mrs_results,
  "High MRS",
  mrs_median,
  unname(reduced_excel_paths["High MRS"])
)
write_reduced_model_excel(
  sf_low,
  low_mrs_results,
  "Low MRS",
  mrs_median,
  unname(reduced_excel_paths["Low MRS"])
)
```

# Full Model with Categorical MRS, Baseline pTau, and Time

This additional model uses the pooled complete, finite observations in
`mrs_model_df`. It uses the same participant-level median split already
defined above, with **Low MRS as the reference group**. MRS enters this
model as `MRS_group`; baseline pTau and time remain continuous. The model
includes all main effects and two-way interactions, the three-way interaction,
the original covariates, and a participant random intercept.

The `MRS_groupHigh MRS:baseline_pTau:time` coefficient estimates the
**High-versus-Low difference in the association between baseline pTau and
annual memory change**. The `baseline_pTau:time` coefficient describes
that association in Low MRS; adding the three-way coefficient gives the
corresponding association in High MRS. A positive three-way estimate means
the pTau-related slope difference is more positive in High MRS. When the
Low-group association is negative, this can weaken, eliminate, or reverse
that association, depending on the sum of the two coefficients.

## Define Model

```{r full_categorical_mrs_formula}
full_mrs_model_df <- mrs_model_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    MRS_group = factor(
      as.character(.data$MRS_group), levels = c("Low MRS", "High MRS")
    )
  )

if (
  anyNA(full_mrs_model_df$MRS_group) ||
  any(table(full_mrs_model_df$MRS_group) == 0L)
) {
  stop("The categorical Full Model requires both Low MRS and High MRS groups.")
}

categorical_formula <- stats::as.formula(
  paste(
    "PHC_MEM ~ baseline_age_z",
    "PHC_Sex",
    "APOE4",
    "PHC_Education",
    "MRS_group * baseline_pTau * time",
    "(1 | RID)",
    sep = " + "
  )
)
```

## Run Model

```{r full_categorical_mrs_model}
sg_mrs_categorical <- lmerTest::lmer(
  categorical_formula,
  data = full_mrs_model_df,
  contrasts = list(MRS_group = "contr.treatment"),
  REML = TRUE,
  na.action = stats::na.fail
)
if (anyNA(lme4::fixef(sg_mrs_categorical, add.dropped = TRUE))) {
  stop(
    "The categorical Full Model has non-estimable fixed effects. ",
    "Inspect the covariate and within-group pTau/time variation."
  )
}
cat("Full Model: categorical Low/High MRS x baseline pTau x time\n")
summary(sg_mrs_categorical)
```

## Test of the Categorical MRS Three-Way Interaction

This one-degree-of-freedom likelihood-ratio test compares two pooled
categorical-MRS models on identical observations. Both are fitted by
maximum likelihood. The comparison model removes only the three-way
interaction and retains all main effects, two-way interactions, covariates,
and the participant random intercept. It is a separate pooled model from
the two dataset-specific Reduced Models above. The REML summary above
and this ML likelihood-ratio test use different inference procedures and
can produce different P values.

```{r categorical_mrs_three_way_test}
sg_mrs_categorical_ml <- stats::update(sg_mrs_categorical, REML = FALSE)
sf_mrs_categorical_ml <- stats::update(
  sg_mrs_categorical_ml,
  . ~ . - MRS_group:baseline_pTau:time
)
stopifnot(
  stats::nobs(sg_mrs_categorical_ml) == stats::nobs(sf_mrs_categorical_ml),
  stats::nobs(sg_mrs_categorical_ml) == nrow(full_mrs_model_df)
)
categorical_mrs_interaction_df <-
  attr(stats::logLik(sg_mrs_categorical_ml), "df") -
  attr(stats::logLik(sf_mrs_categorical_ml), "df")

if (categorical_mrs_interaction_df != 1L) {
  stop(
    "The categorical-MRS three-way interaction is not fully estimable ",
    "(expected one additional parameter)."
  )
}

categorical_mrs_three_way_lrt <- stats::anova(
  sf_mrs_categorical_ml, sg_mrs_categorical_ml, refit = FALSE
)
categorical_mrs_three_way_lrt
```

# Full Model with Continuous MRS, Baseline pTau, and Time

This pooled model uses the same complete, finite observations as the
categorical full model. MRS enters as the continuous `mrs_z` variable on
its original pooled participant-level z-score scale. Baseline pTau retains
its input-data scale, and time is measured in years. The model includes
all main effects, all two-way interactions, the three-way interaction,
the same covariates, and a participant random intercept.

The `mrs_z:baseline_pTau:time` coefficient estimates the change in the
association between baseline pTau and annual memory change per one SD
higher MRS on the original pooled scale. At an MRS z-score of `m`, that
pTau association is `baseline_pTau:time + m * mrs_z:baseline_pTau:time`.
A positive three-way coefficient makes this association more positive
as MRS increases; when the association at lower MRS is negative, this
can represent a weaker association of pTau with faster memory decline.

## Define Model

```{r full_continuous_mrs_formula}
continuous_formula <- stats::as.formula(
  paste(
    "PHC_MEM ~ baseline_age_z",
    "PHC_Sex",
    "APOE4",
    "PHC_Education",
    "mrs_z * baseline_pTau * time",
    "(1 | RID)",
    sep = " + "
  )
)
```

## Run Model

```{r full_continuous_mrs_model}
sg_mrs_continuous <- lmerTest::lmer(
  continuous_formula,
  data = full_mrs_model_df,
  REML = TRUE,
  na.action = stats::na.fail
)

if (anyNA(lme4::fixef(sg_mrs_continuous, add.dropped = TRUE))) {
  stop(
    "The continuous Full Model has non-estimable fixed effects. ",
    "Inspect the covariate and MRS/pTau/time variation."
  )
}

stopifnot(
  stats::nobs(sg_mrs_continuous) == stats::nobs(sg_mrs_categorical),
  identical(
    rownames(stats::model.frame(sg_mrs_continuous)),
    rownames(stats::model.frame(sg_mrs_categorical))
  )
)
cat("Full Model: continuous MRS z x baseline pTau x time\n")
summary(sg_mrs_continuous)
```

## Test of the Continuous MRS Three-Way Interaction

This one-degree-of-freedom likelihood-ratio test compares pooled continuous
MRS models fitted by maximum likelihood on identical observations. The
comparison model removes only `mrs_z:baseline_pTau:time` and retains every
main effect, two-way interaction, covariate, and the random intercept.
The REML summary and ML likelihood-ratio test use different inference
procedures and can produce different P values.

```{r continuous_mrs_three_way_test}
sg_mrs_continuous_ml <- stats::update(sg_mrs_continuous, REML = FALSE)
sf_mrs_continuous_ml <- stats::update(
  sg_mrs_continuous_ml,
  . ~ . - mrs_z:baseline_pTau:time
)
stopifnot(
  stats::nobs(sg_mrs_continuous_ml) == stats::nobs(sf_mrs_continuous_ml),
  stats::nobs(sg_mrs_continuous_ml) == nrow(full_mrs_model_df),
  identical(
    rownames(stats::model.frame(sg_mrs_continuous_ml)),
    rownames(stats::model.frame(sf_mrs_continuous_ml))
  )
)
continuous_mrs_interaction_df <-
  attr(stats::logLik(sg_mrs_continuous_ml), "df") -
  attr(stats::logLik(sf_mrs_continuous_ml), "df")
if (continuous_mrs_interaction_df != 1L) {
  stop(
    "The continuous-MRS three-way interaction is not fully estimable ",
    "(expected one additional parameter)."
  )
}
continuous_mrs_three_way_lrt <- stats::anova(
  sf_mrs_continuous_ml, sg_mrs_continuous_ml, refit = FALSE
)
continuous_mrs_three_way_lrt
```

# Save

```{r save}
saveRDS(
  list(
    sf_low = sf_low,
    sf_high = sf_high,
    sg_mrs_categorical = sg_mrs_categorical,
    sg_mrs_continuous = sg_mrs_continuous
  ),
  file.path(save_dir, "ADNI_Models.rds")
)
cat("Saved:", file.path(save_dir, "ADNI_Models.rds"), "\n")
```
